title: Fetch–decode–execute and buses
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Which register holds the address accessed during a fetch?
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.

questions.answer: The current instruction that is being decoded or executed.

questions.prompt: What kind of information travels along the address bus?
questions.answer: Addresses identifying the memory or device location.
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
Addresses identifying the memory or device location.
Addresses identifying the memory AND device location.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Addresses identifying the memory or device location.

questions.prompt: A rising-edge D flip-flop has Q=0. D changes to 1 between clock edges; the next rising edge occurs while D=1. State Q before and after that edge, and explain why.
questions.answer: Before edge Q stays 0; at rising edge D=1 is sampled so Q becomes 1. It changes on the active edge, not merely when D changes.
options: Before edge Q stays 0; at rising edge D=1 is sampled so Q becomes 1. It changes on the active edge, not merely when D changes.
Before edge Q stays 1; at rising edge D=1 is sampled so Q becomes 1. It changes on the active edge, not merely when D changes.
Before edge Q stays -1; at rising edge D=1 is sampled so Q becomes 1. It changes on the active edge, not merely when D changes.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Before edge Q stays 0; at rising edge D=1 is sampled so Q becomes 1. It changes on the active edge, not merely when D changes.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: fetch — Retrieve next instruction from memory.
data bus — Transfers data and instructions.
control bus — Transfers signals coordinating reads and writes.

blocks.title: Fetch uses the buses
blocks.text: The address bus carries the address selected by MAR; memory returns instruction data on the data bus; control signals coordinate the transfer.

blocks.title: Decode interprets instruction
blocks.text: The control unit examines CIR to decide which operation and operands are involved.

blocks.title: Execute changes state
blocks.text: An instruction may update ACC or memory, or alter PC for a jump. Interrupt handling is coordinated at appropriate points and can temporarily redirect execution.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: MAR identifies location 40; the address bus carries that location to memory, accompanied by a read control signal.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the answer
blocks.text: The data bus transfers instruction content to MDR, then CIR; sequential PC becomes 41.

questions.feedback: fetch — Retrieve next instruction from memory.

blocks.title: Predict first
blocks.text: The initial fetch advances PC from 81 to 82, as in a sequential instruction.

blocks.title: Explain the answer
blocks.text: Executing the unconditional branch overwrites PC with target address 120. The next fetch occurs there, not at 82.
